title: The Dark Farm
checkpoint: Reception Spring 2, week 2 — Learning — Phase 3: new sounds ar, or, ur
note_for_grown_ups: Three more long vowels: oo (as in moon and in good — it does two jobs), ar (farm) and or (corn). Say oo both ways so your child hears that the same team can make a long and a short sound.

pages.text: It was dark on the farm.
pages.illustration: Wide night view of a farm — barn, gate, corn field — under a deep blue sky. Almost no light yet. Establish the whole setting in one picture.

pages.text: Pip sees the moon up high.
pages.illustration: Pip small on a gatepost in the foreground, looking up at a large bright full moon. Strong silhouette against a pale moon disc.

pages.text: The moon is far, far up.
pages.illustration: The same moon, drawn tiny at the top of a mostly empty page, with the farm a thin dark strip along the bottom. Use the empty space to say 'far'.

pages.text: A fox ran to the corn.
pages.illustration: A fox slipping between corn stalks, low and quick, brush held straight out behind it. Only partly visible through the stems. Sharp and beautiful, not frightening.

pages.text: The fox had a bit of corn.
pages.illustration: The fox trotting away with one corn cob in its mouth, glancing back at the reader with a look of complete innocence. Comic.
Ned sitting on a rock pulling off a wellington boot, leaning right back with the effort, tongue out. Very funny physical comedy.

pages.text: He put his foot in the cool pool.
pages.illustration: Ned's bare orange foot lowered into a clear cool pool, ripples spreading, his face pure relief. Cool blues against the warm dark.

pages.text: Soon the sun will be up.
pages.illustration: First light: the sky going pale green-gold at the horizon behind the barn, the moon still faintly up. Quiet and hopeful.

pages.text: Pip and Ned had fun on the farm.
pages.illustration: Closing page: Pip and Ned on the farm gate, sunrise behind them, both facing the new day. Warm gold flooding across the fields.
